timeline.text: Welcome to GoStop Live!
GoStop Live! lets anyone around the world play GoStop together.
Play with friends, the computer, or other players around the globe.
On PC or Mac, click a card once to select it.
The card lifts out of your hand so you can see what is selected.
Click the selected card again to play it onto the table.
When a table choice is required, click the highlighted card you want.
On mobile, tap a card once to select it.
Tap the selected card again to play it.
Or press the card and flick upward for a faster play.
The card follows the upward gesture and plays onto the table.
The game screen is interactive. Tap or click your player area for player information.
Tap the score for a complete scoring breakdown.
Tap your captured-card area to inspect captured cards and scoring groups.
Game controls such as How to Play and Quit Game stay available on the screen.
Training Mode teaches you while you practice against the computer AI.
Friendly Solo Play is casual play against AI with no Coins or ranking.
Play With Friend creates a room link you can send to another person.
Competitive Solo Play lets you play the computer for Coins and ranking.
Competitive Online Play lets you compete with other GoStop Live! players.
Auto Match recommends an available opponent and shows you who you are about to challenge.
You can browse top players or search for a specific player.
Send a Friend Request to connect with players you want to find again.
Friends and recommendations make it easy to start another game together.
The Leaderboards button opens the all-time Global Leaderboard.
Swipe to see this month’s Global Leaderboard.
Competitive wins and losses change your Coins and your global ranking.
If you leave the Main Menu untouched, Attract Mode cycles through the leaderboards automatically.
The goal is simple: match card families, capture scoring cards, reach 7 points, then choose GO or STOP.
Every family has exactly four cards.
GoStop Live! uses twelve easy family names instead of month numbers.
Pine, Plum, Cherry, Vine, Iris, Rose, Bush, Hill, Daisy, Star, Berry, and Willow.
Cards score in four main types: Brights, Pictures, Stripes, and Singles.
Stripes include Red, Blue, and Plain Stripe sets.
Singles are the most common cards.
Some special Single cards count as two Singles.
Brights: three Brights with the Rain Bright score 2 points. Three non-Rain Brights score 3.
Four Brights score 4 points, and all five Brights score 15 points.
5-BIRDIES! scores 5 points. Any five Pictures score 1 point, then each extra Picture adds 1.
Three Red, Blue, or Plain Stripes score 3 points. Any five Stripes score 1, then each extra Stripe adds 1.
Ten Singles score 1 point, then each extra Single adds 1. 2x Single cards count as two.
A turn starts by playing one card from your hand.
If the table has one card from the same family, your played card captures it.
Then the draw pile flips one card.
If the drawn card matches a table family, it captures that card too.
If there is no match, the played or drawn card stays on the table.
At 7 points in a two-player game, you choose GO or STOP.
STOP ends the hand and you take the points you have now.
GO keeps the game going. The first GO adds 1 point, and the second GO adds another point.
From the third GO onward, the settlement doubles with each additional GO.
If you lose after declaring GO, your opponent also receives the GO penalty multiplier.
SHAKE: reveal three cards from the same family. A normal Shake doubles your settlement if you win.
BOMB: keep three same-family cards hidden. When the fourth is on the table, play all three, capture the family, and steal one Single.
POOPED! is 뻑. Your play and the draw create a three-card family stack. Capturing it later steals one Single.
KISS! is 쪽. Your played card has no match, then the draw gives the matching family. Capture the pair and steal one Single.
FLUSH! is 따닥, and CLEAN SWEEP! is 싹쓸이. These special captures also steal one Single when available.
You do not need to memorize everything. Full Rules keeps the complete written reference one click away.
Your best first game is Training Mode.
Play against AI while GoStop Live! highlights a recommended card and table target.
Training Mode explains why the move is recommended and teaches special rules as they happen.
Have fun playing GoStop Live!
